Hello there flipper of finds, thrifter of threads!

This subverse is dedicated to discussing flipping of every kind and is meant to serve the needs of any flippers on the Voat community.

Below are some rules and basic ideas to get you started, as always, google is your friend:

I want to get started in flipping, but I don't know how?

Here are some ways to get started.

Low Risk/Low Investment

Flipping clothing from a thrift store, Goodwill or yardsale on Ebay or Amazon.

  • Cost to get started varies.

  • Inexpensive to start at thrift stores.

  • May take a while to sell

  • Takes more time to find items worth selling, more legwork and "elbow grease"

  • Must be approved to sell clothing if you sell on Amazon.

Selling books, textbooks and media on Amazon FBA

  • $Free - $100 to get started.

  • May take longer to sell.

  • Must be accurate when listing.

  • Get acquainted with how to use Fulfillment By Amazon.

Hardwood furniture

  • $5 haggle or curbside pickup - $varies depending on piece

  • Find hardwood, non-upholstered furniture at yardsales and flip on craigslist.

  • Best to stick to non-stained, non-painted pieces. If it has paint, buff it off and, at most, give it some clear wood finish.

  • Must have a place to keep the pieces between flips.

Higher Risk/Greater Investment

Retail Arbitrage through Amazon FBA

  • Be ready to put $400 into inventory to get started with your first inbound shipment.

  • Give yourself price wiggle room, stick to >60% ROI.

  • Stick to the top 1% sales rank for a quick sale (i.e. 30k and below for toys, under 200k for home and garden)

  • Look for clearance racks and make sure you pay what was on the label.

  • Make sure you are approved to sell it by looking it up in the Amazon Seller's App.

Private Label / Import

  • $500 - $10k USD

  • Make sure you request a sample from your supplier. If you are selling knockoffs, Amazon will ban you.

  • Make sure you answer customer service emails quickly.

Selling Mediums

Amazon MF

  • Exactly what is sounds like. Amazon sells your product, charges a referral fee, charges a shipping credit to buyer that is passed to you and you fulfill the order.

  • Amazon's fees are high but items sell very fast. Like selling on an online store.

Amazon FBA

  • Fulfillment By Amazon is a program where you prep and ship your items into Amazon's warehouses with UPS Partner shipping rates (typically 1/2 of what UPS would charge) and Amazon fulfills your order and ships it.

  • Items qualify for prime free 2 day shipping and your listings get a pretty little blue "Prime" checkmark, which helps them sell faster and for more money.

  • Costs more money for pick and pack fees.

  • Items must be properly prepped and labeled.

  • Must pay Amazon to fulfill your item through "Multi Channel Fulfillment" if you decide to sell on Ebay instead. MFA can be just as expensive as selling it on Amazon itself.

Ebay

  • Low fees, but items take longer to sell and there is less standardization. More like an auction house or yardsale than a store.

  • Ebay "Concierge" can fulfill your order, but is relatively new and most sales are fulfilled by the seller.

Sub Rules

This is a friendly sub. I will not infringe on your free speech and you will post as a reasonable adult. Nothing further needs to be said about that. Here are some further guidelines.

  1. Refrain from posting personal information. For instance, if you post a picture of a package, black out the address with a graphical editor program.

  2. Do not try to sell products to this sub. If you have a product to sell, like an app, contact a moderator and I will approve the post.

  3. Information is give and take. The best compensation for someone's lesson from the school of hard knocks is payment in useful information.
